31 December
On this day in 1612

Guru Hargobind left Amritsar for Delhi where he was taken into and sent to Gwalior

31 December brings together four moments of Sikh history, from 1612 to 1958. The main event of the day is from 1612: Guru Hargobind left Amritsar for Delhi where he was taken into and sent to Gwalior. Together they span four periods, from Miri-Piri and the middle Gurus (1606–1674) to The Punjabi Suba movement (1948–1966). People, places and movements connected with this day include Guru Hargobind Sahib Ji, Amritsar, Delhi and Sri Harmandir Sahib (Darbar Sahib).

Historical background

Miri-Piri and the middle Gurus (1606–1674)

After the martyrdom of Guru Arjan Dev Ji in 1606, Guru Hargobind Sahib Ji wore two swords of miri and piri (temporal and spiritual authority), established the Akal Takht and fought several engagements with Mughal forces. The seventh and eighth Gurus, Guru Har Rai Ji and Guru Har Krishan Ji, led the community from Kiratpur and Delhi, and Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji founded Anandpur (Chak Nanaki) in 1665.

On this day in this period: 1612 Guru Hargobind left Amritsar for Delhi where he was taken into and sent to Gwalior.

The Gurdwara Reform (Akali) movement (1920–1925)

Sikhs organised the Shiromani Gurdwara Parbandhak Committee (November 1920) and the Shiromani Akali Dal (December 1920) to free historic gurdwaras from hereditary mahants backed by the government. Through non-violent morchas, including Nankana Sahib (1921), the keys agitation (1921–22), Guru ka Bagh (1922) and Jaito (1923–25), and alongside the militant Babbar Akali movement, the campaign led to the Sikh Gurdwaras Act of 1925.

On this day in this period: 1925 Haji Mohamad Maskeen offered a "Choar" for Sri Darbar Sahib.

Late colonial Punjab and Partition (1926–1947)

With the SGPC established by law, Sikh politics was led by the Akali Dal under figures such as Master Tara Singh and Baba Kharak Singh. Sikhs took part in the freedom movement and in both World Wars, and the Partition of Punjab in August 1947 divided the Sikh homeland, leaving Nankana Sahib and many historic shrines in Pakistan and uprooting millions of Sikhs.

On this day in this period: 1929 Congress Convention at Amritsar ignored by the Sikhs.

The Punjabi Suba movement (1948–1966)

In independent India the Akali Dal campaigned for a Punjabi-speaking state, the Punjabi Suba, through repeated morchas led by Master Tara Singh and Sant Fateh Singh. The demand was met with the reorganisation of Punjab on 1 November 1966, which created present-day Punjab, Haryana and transferred hill areas to Himachal Pradesh.

On this day in this period: 1958 Gurudwara Amendment Bill passed.

People and places of this day

Guru Hargobind Sahib Ji

The sixth Guru (1595–1644), who wore the swords of miri and piri, built the Akal Takht in 1606, was held in Gwalior Fort and released with 52 rajas (remembered as Bandi Chhor Diwas), and fought several battles with Mughal forces before settling at Kiratpur.

Read more → · Mentioned on 20 other days of the year

Amritsar

The city founded by Guru Ram Das Ji around the sacred pool of Amritsar. As the home of Sri Harmandir Sahib and the Akal Takht it has been the spiritual and political centre of the Sikhs for four centuries.

Read more → · Mentioned on 69 other days of the year

Delhi

The Mughal capital, where Guru Har Krishan Ji died (Gurdwara Bangla Sahib), Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji was executed (Gurdwara Sis Ganj Sahib) and Banda Singh Bahadur was put to death in 1716. Baghel Singh's forces entered the city in 1783 and marked its Sikh sites.

Read more → · Mentioned on 36 other days of the year

Sri Harmandir Sahib (Darbar Sahib)

The central Sikh shrine in Amritsar, built by Guru Arjan Dev Ji in the middle of the sacred pool, where the Adi Granth was installed in 1604. Destroyed by Ahmad Shah Abdali and rebuilt, it was covered in gold under Maharaja Ranjit Singh and has been at the centre of many events in Sikh history.
